messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#45678 for service `inference-canary`
incident-bot: Summary: 5m 5xx-rate threshold exceeded for canary traffic. Metric: canary_service.5xx_rate = 2.4% (threshold 0.5%). Link: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/45678 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident created: https://pd.redwood/incident/45678 - policy `canary-5xx-threshold`
emily: ack - i'm on-call and taking ownership
oncall-aws: acked — pulling logs from canary nodes now, checking whether it's infra or app
raj: i'm on pager and starting distributed traces, looks correlated with the new rate-limiter change rolled in this morning to the canary image
emily: can someone pause the rollout? don't want more traffic hitting the canary until we confirm
ops-bot: Suggestion: toggle feature flag `canary_rollout` -> off to stop traffic routing to canary
emily: pausing rollout via flags service now
emily: command:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAGS_TOKEN' \\n  -d '{"flag":"canary_rollout","state":"off"}'
```
emily: flag toggle succeeded, traffic should stop shifting to canary within ~30s :white_check_mark:
raj: pulling app logs — seeing a spike of 429s from internal rate-limiter which then cascades to 5xx when downstream retry logic misbehaves. snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:12:45Z canary-123 app ERROR request_id=xyz status=429 reason="rate_limit_exceeded"
2026-03-15T02:12:46Z canary-123 app ERROR request_id=xyz status=502 reason="upstream_timeout"
```
mike: thanks. if it's the new rate-limiter config, we should roll the canary back to previous image and run a hotfix for the config in a staging branch
olivia: customer impact: so far internal metrics show ~0.1% of total production requests hit canary but a paid beta customer reported ~5% failures for embedding requests in the last 10m. Ops is reaching out to their SRE contact to notify (low-medium impact)
oncall-aws: confirming: traffic diverted back to stable, p95 latency on stable unchanged. canary error-rate trending down after flag toggle
raj: i'll perform rollback to previous canary image for safety. rolling back to image sha `abc123`
raj: command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-canary --to-revision=2
```
raj: rollback started — watching pods
emily: opening a short on-call bridge for coordination: https://meet.redwood/bridge/PD45678
mike: assigning incident commander to raj for now. raj, please coordinate post-rollback verification and handoff when stable
raj: accepted. running smoke tests against stable endpoints and re-checking integrations with rate-limiter
olivia: i've messaged the beta customer with a brief note: "We're aware of increased failures for embedding requests in the last 10 minutes tied to a canary rollout. We've paused the rollout and are reverting the canary. We'll follow up with timelines and root cause."
ops-bot: quick check: autoscaler logs show no node OOMs, no GPU failures, no region-wide degradation
emily: metrics update: canary 5xx rate dropped to 0.08% within 3 minutes of flag toggle and rollback is progressing to stable state
raj: all canary pods back to the previous revision and passing readiness probes. smoke suite green. incremental traffic will stay on stable until we push a vetted config
mike: good. closing the page in PD once we confirm customer-facing issues cleared. raj, please post a short incident summary and action items here when you have a minute
raj: summary draft: "Canary rollout introduced a new rate-limiter config that mis-applied limits for high-concurrency paths, leading to 429s and follow-on 5xx due to retries. We paused the rollout via feature flag and rolled back the canary to the prior image. Immediate impact limited to a small subset of beta traffic; stable unaffected."
olivia: action items: 1) reproduce locally and write a unit test for rate-limiter boundary behavior; 2) add canary-specific monitor to detect 429->5xx cascading; 3) update rollout runbook to include feature-flag pause steps and a rollback checklist. I'll create tickets
emily: PD incident closed by me after observation window; will transition to follow-up channel `#postmortems` for write-up
ops-bot: note added: runbook link https://docs.redwood/runbooks/canary-rollouts and playbook snippet for flag toggle included
mike: thanks everyone. good quick triage and coordination. we'll sync in the 1pm blameless postmortem to review change gating and alerts thresholds. :bow:
